correctness.rationale: For a fixed zero-sum nonzero mortality perturbation, the pairwise equilibrium and reduced-Jacobian trace are exact polynomials, confirmed by symbolic identities. The base determinant q²/3 is positive; the homogeneous trace is -q²α/3; cyclic invariance forces the first ε derivative to vanish for all α. Analytic implicit-function arguments give the unique nearby trace crossing and cubic coefficient; the determinant and trace signs give local linear classification. Numerical tests corroborate but do not prove infinite-domain steps. No global/Hopf cycle assertions.

value.rationale: The initiating article analyzes critical higher-order fractions using mortality variance. This exact statement identifies a mathematically motivated omitted invariant: a signed oriented Vandermonde distinguishing mortality assignments with identical means, variance and full unordered distribution. It is the first possible odd-permutation contribution, appears at cubic order in weak differences, and changes a biologically interpretable local stabilization threshold. A two-assignment example proves why no unordered demographic summary suffices; the claim is not a trivial rescaling of the known quadratic trend.
